turns.prompt_text: does a machine exist that can scan a book
turns.response_html:
Yes, several types of machines are specifically designed to scan books without damaging their spines. These range from affordable consumer devices to high-end industrial robots.

Common Types of Book Scanners

  • Overhead Scanners: These use a camera mounted above a flat surface to take pictures of the book while it lies face-up. Many include software to automatically "flatten" the curvature of the pages and remove images of your fingers holding the edges.
  • V-Cradle Scanners: These hold the book in a V-shape to prevent the spine from being overextended. They are often used for fragile historical texts.
  • Automatic Robotic Scanners: Used by large libraries and archives (like Google Books), these machines use vacuum suction or "bionic fingers" to automatically turn the pages at speeds of up to 2,500 pages per hour.
  • Flatbed Book Scanners: These look like standard scanners but have a "zero-edge" design, allowing the book's spine to hang off the side so the page can lay perfectly flat against the glass.
